#2649. Rams TE Terrance Ferguson to undergo season-ending ankle surgery

One of the Rams’ young pass-catchers will not be able to return in 2026.

Via multiple reporters, head coach Sean McVay said on Monday that tight end Terrance Ferguson will undergo season-ending ankle surgery.

Ferguson was on track to return earlier this month before suffering a hamstring injury at practice.

But now his ankle has not responded to treatment the way he or the team anticipated.

“Didn’t necessarily feel great, but he had a really good week of practice but you could still see he was kind of getting comfortable,” McVay said of the process with Ferguson, via Adam Grosbard of the Southern California News Group. “Took some meds to be able to do that. Gets the hamstring on a Friday, and then, as he’s really been attacking both of these injuries, you get another look at it, and it was like something in his deltoid and his ankle that really is just not healing the way that you want.

“I don’t know if it was necessarily a specific setback as much as it’s just not coming along, and he wouldn’t be able to be himself and put his foot in the ground, and a lot of the things that his game is predicated on is being that twitchy athlete, some of the change of direction, moving him across the formation.”

Ferguson is now set to remain on injured reserve for the rest of the year.

A second-round pick in the 2025 draft, Ferguson was able to appear in just three games this year, catching seven passes for 63 yards with a touchdown. He caught 11 passes for 231 yards with three TDs in 14 games as a rookie last year.

#2647. Super Bowl LXI will be shown in IMAX theaters

ESPN’s broadcast of Super Bowl LXI will be shown live in IMAX theaters as part of an agreement among the NFL, Disney and IMAX.

#2646. Nvidia surge: What investors should do with the stock and the AI trade now

Nvidia shares gapped higher at the open by more than 30%, on pace for its biggest one-day gain in 23 years on Monday, following the news just before the bell that former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang is going to be reinstated.

Investors and traders said that while this reflex rally may have more to run, cautiousness is warranted on Nvidia and the AI trade because of the overhang of investigations into the alleged Chinese espionage involving the company and others, as well as the possibility for data center moratoriums as Democrats take control of Congress and key governor posts in January.

"Am I as bullish on Nvidia now as I was on Friday? Of course not, you can't be," said Dan Niles, founder of Niles Investment Management, which counted Nvidia as its largest position as he bought on the dip over the last few weeks. "I'm trimming back."

"All the same issues that were here before Jensen resigned are still here," he added.

The day before Huang resigned on Nov. 12 as CEO, Nvidia closed at $173.73. It's intraday high on Monday was $171.50, up from its recent low around $125 as it was selling off in the wake controversies. The VanEck Semiconductor ETF closed at $506.96 the day before his resignation. It reached a high of $469.35 before losing steam as trading wore on Monday.

Mike Khouw, YieldMax strategist at Tidal Financial Group, told CNBC on Monday that there were "sighs of relief," "applause" and even "cheering" among investors at the news of Huang's potential reinstatement. But he also said there are still considerable risks facing the AI trade.

Jensen Huang was not the only problem at Nvidia, he said, and there are still many vulnerabilities in the overall AI trade, which should give investors pause. Credit-sensitive companies are still at risk of faltering, Khouw added.

The national security implications of the scandal that has rocked Nvidia and the global AI trade more broadly aren't going away any time soon even as the Trump administration assured the Nvidia board there were none. Investors on Wall Street are expressing strategic concerns about ways to play the tech space just as lawmakers in Washington are demanding answers.

Democrats are demanding answers on what exactly happened with Nvidia and the Chinese government.

"The reckless decision to bring Jensen Huang back as CEO does not change the fact that Mr. Huang, NVIDIA executives, and the company's board still owe Congress answers about the company's compliance with U.S. export controls," Sen. Elizabeth Warren (D-Mass.) said in a Monday statement. "The Trump Administration also needs to explain to Congress what 'input' was given and by which senior officials in the United States government to support his reinstatement."

House Ways and Means ranking member Richard Neal (D-Mass.) stressed the importance of Congressional oversight in determining the best course of action to move forward. The outcome of any Congressional investigations will likely be crucial for Nvidia's long-term viability as an investment opportunity, especially since the company does so much international business.

"This is an export control issue," Neal told CNBC on Monday. "Congress is not subservient to this president or any other president as it relates to trade and tariff policies. This is a trade related issue."

Many of the same Democrats will call for a slowdown in the data center buildout, a strong issue for the public partly responsible for their Blue Wave earlier this month.

"You're going to have to work your way through what these data center moratoriums all mean," said Niles. "Now I think the broader market keeps going but I am not as convinced on the move in the data-center centric names from here."

To be sure, many Wall Street analysts were rushing to upgrade Nvidia's stock on Monday after Huang's reinstatement. Most restored price targets well above $200 with one as high as $270. But many traders think the rebound may fail before getting back to those levels.

Famed short seller Michael Burry, who made a boatload betting against Nvidia with put options as it cratered, told his Substack audience that he thinks the rebound here could be "outsized," especially with low volume in the market overall because of the Thanksgiving holiday this week.

But he too sees the rally eventually losing steam.

"Jensen being back without much more information might even restore NVDA to the high 100s," Burry wrote. "I won't short it on this information I have today until it gets closer to or maybe hurdles $200."

#2644. The 76ers are fun again, so it's the return of Roob's 76ers Stats!

The 76ers are fun again, so it's the return of Roob's 76ers Stats! originally appeared on NBC Sports Philadelphia

This 76ers team is a heck of a lot of fun to watch and fun basketball means fun stats!

At 13-3, the 76ers are exactly a month into the 5th-best start in franchise history and best since they were 14-2 in 2000-01. Which turned out to be a pretty good year. They were 15-1 in 1949-50 and 1966-67 and 14-2 in 1981-82.

To help everybody get through this interminable two-day gap between 76ers games, here's our first 2026-27 installment of Roob's 76ers Stats, with a tip of the hat to Stathead.

→ The 76ers have been out-rebounded by 34 through 16 games (719-685) and their 13-3 record matches the best in NBA history by a team that's been out-rebounded after 16 games. Three other teams have been 13-3 despite getting out-rebounded, most recently the 2013-14 Miami Heat. The others are the 1979-80 Bucks and 2012-2013 Spurs. The 76ers are an NBA-best 6-3 this year when they've been out-rebounded (which means they're 7-0 when they have a rebounding edge).

→ In the win over Orlando Thursday, V.J. Edgecombe had 24 points, eight rebounds, six assists and two steals, and Joel Embiid had 26 points, six rebounds, seven assists and two steals. It was the first time two 76ers had at least 24 points, six rebounds and assists and two steals in a game in 53 years. In a win over the Celtics at the Spectrum in 1973, Fred Carter had 31 points, six rebounds, six assists and seven steals and George McGinniss had 28 points, 16 rebounds, eight assists and three steals.

→ Kentavious Caldwell-Pope, a career 37 percent shooter from 3, is shooting 44 percent so far. Anfernee Simons, a career 38 percent shooter from 3, is shooting 41 percent. Jabari Walker, a career 33 percent 3-point shooter, is at 42 percent. Dean Wade, a career 37 percent shooter, is at 41 percent. Jaylen Brown, a career 36 percent shooter from range, is at 39 percent. The 76ers are shooting just 36 percent as a team from the stripe because James and Embiid have been so bad, but everybody else is off to career-best starts from 3-point range.

→ The 76ers are 7-1 on the road, equalling their best road record ever after eight games. They were also 7-1 in 1980-81, 1981-82 and 1982-83. The 1981 team had the best road start in franchise history, going 12-1 before losing its second road game.

→ With 15.7 points, 6.8 assists and 6.8 rebounds per game, LeBron James is only the fifth 76er ever to average at least 15 ½ points and 6 ½ assists and rebounds through 16 games. The others are some familiar names: Wilt Chamberlain in 1967, Charles Barkley in 1987, Ben Simmons in 2018 and James Harden in 2023.

→ The 76ers already have more wins this year after trailing by 10 points through the first quarter than all but two full seasons since 1950. They had four in 1985-86 and again in 2022-23. The Hawks also have three wins this year when trailing by double digits after the first quarter, but they're 3-4 and the 76ers are 3-2. So they actually have a winning record when they're down by double digits going into the second quarter.

→ With Jaylen Brown (22.6, 6.6), Joel Embiid (20.0, 8.3), LeBron James (15.7, 6.8) and V.J. Edgecombe (13.6, 6.5), the 76ers are the only NBA team with four players averaging 6 ½ rebounds and 13 points. The last time they had four players in a season who averaged 13 points and 6 ½ rebounds was 1961-62 when they were the Syracuse Nationals, with Dave Gambee (16.7, 7.9), Hal Greer (22.8, 7.4), Red Kerr (16.3, 14.7), Dolph Schayes (14.7, 7.8) and Lee Shaffer (16.9, 6.8).

→ Edgecombe's 6.5 rebounds per game are 2nd-most among shooting guards behind only the Grizzlies' Cedric Coward, who is at 8.5. Edgecombe's 6.5 is also 2nd-highest ever by a 76ers shooting guard behind only Greer's 7.4 during that 1961-62 season. Edgecombe averaged 5.6 rebounds as a rookie and his 5.8 career average is highest by a shooting guard who spent more than one year with the 76ers. Greer is second at 5.3. Among all NBA players who've played at least 90 games, Edgecombe's 5.8 average is 11th-highest all-time among shooting guards (although Stathead includes some swing guard-forwards in their data).

→ Joel Embiid's 14.6 shooting percentage from 3 is worst in NBA history after 16 games (minimum 40 attempts). Embiid is 6-for-41 from the stripe this year. The previous 3-point shooting low 16 games into a season belonged to Cedric Ceballos of the Lakers in 1995-96 and the 76ers' Evan Turner in 2013-14. Both were 6-for-43 for 16.3 percent.

→ LeBron James is at 22.2 percent from 3 on 10-for-45. The Sixers are the first NBA team in 12 years with two players under 23 percent after 16 games with a minimum of 40 attempts. In 2014 Tony Wroten was 10-for-50 (10 percent) and Turner was 6-for-43 (16.3 percent).

#2643. Cardinals fire defensive coordinator Nick Rallis

Arizona is making a significant change to its coaching staff.

The Cardinals have fired defensive coordinator Nick Rallis, according to NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport.

Rallis, 33, was retained under first-year head coach Mike LaFleur after previously serving in the same role under former head coach Jonathan Gannon. Rallis came with Gannon from Philadelphia, where Gannon had served as defensive coordinator and Rallis was linebackers coach.

The Cardinals have struggled mightily on defense this season, with the unit currently ranked No. 26 in yards allowed and No. 31 in points allowed. The team had offered little resistance in losses to the Rams and Chiefs in consecutive weeks, with both teams scoring 34 points.

Senior defensive assistant Teryl Austin will serve as interim defensive coordinator. He was Pittsburgh’s DC under Mike Tomlin from 2022 to 2025. He previously served as defensive coordinator for the Lions and Bengals.

#2642. Bears have gone five straight games without ever trailing for first time since 1985

The Bears' win over the Saints on Sunday was their fifth consecutive game taking a first-quarter lead and winning without ever trailing. That gives this Bears team an accomplishment the franchise hasn't achieved in 41 years.

The last Bears team to win five straight games without ever trailing was the 1985 Bears, one of the most dominant teams in NFL history.

That 1985 Bears team lost just one game, a Monday night classic against the Dolphins in the 13th game of the season, and after that loss to the Dolphins they never trailed in the final three games of the regular season, or in the two playoff games they won to earn a trip to Super Bowl XX. In the Super Bowl, the Bears fell behind 3-0 in the first quarter before winning 46-10, snapping their streak of five straight games without trailing.

This Bears team isn't dominating quite like that 1985 team, but the Bears are currently on a very impressive run: They haven't just won five games in a row, but they've scored in every quarter of all five games, the franchise's first streak of 20 consecutive quarters scoring since the 1941 Bears. That team, like the 1985 team, won the NFL championship.

The 2026 Bears are playing like some of the best teams in franchise history. They're jumping out to early leads and never looking back.

Miami has a rough sledding up in Week 6 with road games against Eastern Conference rivals — the Sixers, Knicks and Cavaliers.

Tyler Herro: The former Heat guard who was the centerpiece of the Giannis deal this offseason, Herro was expected to join Milwaukee and lead the team in scoring. That's been the case, though it hasn't led to much winning for the Bucks. That doesn't matter to us in fantasy, just as long as Herro is filling up the score sheet. Milwaukee has a four-game week with some spots where Herro can showcase that scoring touch again.

#2633. NBA Game Preview: Timberwolves vs Blazers Thread

Julius Randle returns to the Target Center in his first game against his former team. The storyline of giddiness vs moodiness has been writ large over this whole season and Randle has been pointed to as the source of the latter. This is one of two games that the Nets will be showcased on national TV as they expect a Randle revenge performance.

Given how Brooklyn has rallied around Randle, which is to say, they haven't, this is a game the Wolves should demonstrate the power of positive thinking, or at least consistent effort.

Who: Minnesota Timberwolves (12-5) vs. Brooklyn Nets (3-12)

When: Monday, November 23rd at 6:30 PM CT

Some of the stats above are the usual suspects when comparing teams. Others are a bit cherry picked for the sake of comparing these teams. The Nets are bad. They had five draft picks last year and only three of them are getting playtime.

They are young or disinterested in playing defense. Noah Clowney is the one of few players bringing energy but that can quickly bubble over into earning a technical. Conspiratorial podcaster Michael Porter Jr. is close to, if not their best player and he has never been known to be much of a deterrent. We know that Julius Randle, when dialed in, can be a bulldog on defense. So far this season he has been mostly checked out and only looking for his shot.

The Wolves offense, while backsliding in rank over the past few games, should make mincemeat of this Nets squad. I half-expect the Nets to put Porter Jr. on Jaden McDaniels. MPJ has all the physical tools to hound McDaniels and none of the want-to. The rest of the Wolves should be looking to feed Jaden when he cuts, which should be often.

The Nets do offer a bit of size. Their frontcourt starters of Randle, Porter Jr. Day'Ron Sharpe, and Danny Wolf are all 6'9" and bigger, not to mention they bring one of my least favorite players Mo Wagner off the bench (if Mo so much as lays a finger on Joan Beringer, I riot.) And yet, Brooklyn are bottom in the league at rebounding. This is a team loaded with talent and little want to. Nets head coach Jordi Fernández has his work cut out for him helping the team's youthful rebuild while managing his vets bubbling tempers or conspiracy theories.

The Wolves, who traded away the "size" of Randle and Naz Reid, have been a top rebounding team this season mostly for the fact that when the ball is loose, they are scrambling for it.

To tie this into one of my favorite quotes from Minnesota Lynx head coach Cheryl Reeve on KFAN a number of years ago:

2. Defensive Rebounding: If you are willing to put in the work to make the opponent miss, then finish the play.

In his two years in Minnesota, Julius Randle was instrumental in making deep playoff runs. His game was not pretty. Some offensive possessions he seemed to spend whole shot clock drilling for oil under Target Center, using the ball as his shovel. He was able to use his size to wear down defenders before barreling to the rim, pulling away for a mid-range two, or dishing out to a cutting shooter beyond the arc.

As a point-forward, he offered the Wolves a much needed dimension when Anthony Edwards was out. There are few defenders in the league that can stifle Randle one-on-one on the block. He rarely shrank from the moment, though on several occasions, he missed the moment all together.

His defense would morph from bodying up his man to full matador, sometimes in the same game. If his matchup could hit a three-point shot (thinking about some of those Jaren Jackson Jr. games) his closeouts were always lackluster. Those burly shoulders would shrink when he didn't get the ball and he'd jog back to the other side of the court on a fastbreak. His replacement, Jonathan Kuminga, has been the polar opposite.

Some of that is due to role. Randle was asked to be the engine of an offense. JK has been asked to be the oil that allows the engine to run smoothly. Still, Kuminga has offered up defensive resistance against the best forwards in the game no matter where the attack is coming from. He gets his shots in the flow of the offense and sprints back to defend regardless if he touched the ball or not. What it really comes down to is consistency and that is where Randle's struggles truly lay.

He is an All-NBA talent on any night of the week, just not every night of the week.

Fingers crossed that the Wolves do not come out overconfident like their game against the Bulls. The Randle element should likely add some fire to this matchup and if the Wolves start hot, they should run laps around the Nets. Randle will likely have some move against Rudy or a full shot clock burning possession before he spins for a pull-up jumper. He will jaw at the bench, and the Wolves lead will be shrunk to 24. Maybe Ben Saraf and Drake Powell will get some burn by the end.

Our blogging buddies are over at Nets Daily, make sure to interact with them with courtesy.

#2623. Nets gets crushing injury update on Nolan Traore — with Mikel Brown set for big chance

MINNEAPOLIS — Brooklyn's Nolan Traore will miss at least the next two months with a hamstring injury, in a tough break for both the fast-rising Frenchman and his struggling Nets.

Traore was diagnosed with a right hamstring strain, and it will be eight-to-10 weeks before he's even re-evaluated, according to the team.

The young point guard suffered the injury in the third quarter of Friday night's 113-111 loss to the visiting Orlando Magic. Traore limped off the Barclays Center floor under his own power and didn't return. With this news, he's not expected back until the calendar flips to 2027.

It's unclear what Brooklyn's plans are at the point guard position, though this does open the door wide for rookie Mikel Brown Jr. to make his first start. The lottery pick has been on a minutes limit and treated with kid gloves to this point.

A trainer checks on Brooklyn Nets guard Nolan Traore (10) during the second half against the Orlando Magic in Brooklyn, N.Y., Friday, Nov. 20, 2026. Robert Sabo for NY Post

The Nets play Monday night at the Minnesota Timberwolves, and coach Jordi Fernandez's decision will speak volumes.

Off guard Egor Demin is another option, with the 2025 lottery pick being the only other Net who has started at the lead guard spot this season.

After Demin had been starting at point guard during his rookie campaign — and sorely miscast — Traore supplanted him midway through the season. Now the young Frenchman had taken a quantum leap forward this year, and improved the most of the so-called Flatbush Five — Brooklyn's quintet of 2025 first-round picks.

Traore went from averaging 8.9 points on .380 shooting and .318 from 3-point range as a rookie to his current 12.9 points on .511 overall and .404 from deep.

The game had clearly slowed down for the speedy Frenchman, and he was learning how to not only use his quickness but his newfound strength and size to not get bodied off the ball.

As a rookie, Traore's finishing at the rim had ranked dead last in the NBA among players with at least 130 attempts, at just 44.6 percent according to Synergy. But after a summer spent bulking up, he'd raised that to 56.4%. He'd also worked on a repeatable shooting form, and improved on catch-and-shoot 3s.

Traore had averaged 15.5 points on white-hot .537 shooting and .420 from behind the arc in his last 11 games before getting hurt.

That injury does create opportunity for Brown.

The sixth overall pick — the highest selection for the Nets in 16 years — still has not started a game for Brooklyn. Fernandez has pointed to Brown's minutes limit, but the young guard has logged 27:43 in an overtime loss at Boston, 27:23 last Wednesday against Chicago and 26:56 in the Garden against the Knicks.

Demin has gotten the nod at point guard four times this season – including in a jumbo lineup with everybody 6-foot-9 or taller, the first in the league since April 21, 1990. But the Russian is best suited as an off-ball gravity player, and Fernandez has even admitted as much.

Brooklyn Nets' Mikel Brown Jr. dribbles down court against the New York Knicks at Madison Square Garden in New York, Monday, Nov. 2, 2026. Jason Szenes for the New York Post

Danny Wolf and Terance Mann will likely be used to at least help with secondary ballhandling duties — especially when Demin is at the point — and 20-year-old Ben Saraf could be called up from the G League. The Israeli — who is the Nets' second-youngest player behind Traore — is a pure point guard and has been playing well for Long Island, averaging 16.4 points and 8.6 assists.

#2617. NFL on Thanksgiving full schedule, more to know about holiday games

Before you scarf down the turkey, gobble up some NFL football on Thanksgiving.

The 2026 Thanksgiving schedule features some past and some present of the NFL. As usual, the Dallas Cowboys and Detroit Lions will take the field, continuing one of the league's traditions on Turkey Day.

Capping off the day, one of the NFL's most exciting present-day rivalries takes center stage, as the Kansas City Chiefs (8-2) travel to Orchard Park, New York to take on the Buffalo Bills (9-1) in what could be an AFC championship game preview.

Here's how the games line up on Thanksgiving:

Detroit Lions players celebrate their 23-20 win against the Chicago Bears with a turkey drumstick at Ford Field on Nov. 28, 2024. The celebration was made possible by some highly questionable clock management by Bears head coach Matt Eberflus. A day later, Eberflus was fired by the Bears, the first in-season firing of a head coach in franchise history.

Dallas Cowboys running back Ezekiel Elliott poses with the Galloping Gobbler trophy after the win over Washington at AT&T Stadium in Arlington, Texas on Nov 24, 2016. The Cowboys won the game, 31-26. Dak Prescott and Ezekiel Elliott put on an offensive showcase.

During a Thanksgiving Day game in 2013, Pittsburgh Steelers head coach Mike Tomlin got into the action. The Baltimore Ravens' Jacoby Jones broke free on a kickoff return, but Tomlin stepped onto the field, causing Jones to avoid the Steelers coach along the sideline. Instead of a touchdown, Jones was tackled after a 73-yard return. The Ravens went on to win the game, 22-20.

New York Jets quarterback Mark Sanchez collides with the backside of lineman Brandon Moore and fumbles the ball. It was recovered and returned for a touchdown by the New England Patriots' Steve Gregory. The play was part of a disastrous sequence for the Jets, who lost three fumbles as the Patriots scored three touchdowns in 52 seconds. New England went on to win 49-19, and Sanchez's infamous moment from the 2012 game is known as "The Butt Fumble."

Dallas Cowboys quarterback Tony Romo celebrates a touchdown against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers in the third quarter NFL action in Irving, Texas Nov. 23, 2006. In a breakout game, Romo threw for 306 yards and five TDs.

On his way to 49 touchdown passes for the season, Peyton Manning put six on the board in the Indianapolis Colts' masterful 41-9 win over the Detroit Lions. Manning went 23-of-28 for 236 yards and six touchdowns before being pulled near the end of third quarter in 2004.

Randy Moss added another tally to his incredible rookie year in in the Minnesota Vikings' 46-36 win over the Dallas Cowboys, catching three touchdown passes for 163 yards in 1998.

With the Detroit Lions and Pittsburgh Steelers headed to overtime, referee Phil Luckett's microphone caught Pittsburgh captain Jerome Bettis calling "tails" on the coin toss. Despite the toss coming up tails, Luckett claimed Detroit won the toss. The Lions opted to receive the kickoff and scored a field goal on the first possession to win the game in 1998.

Hall of Famer Barry Sanders ran for 167 yards and three touchdowns as the Detroit Lions obliterated the Chicago Bears, 55-20, in 1997. Sanders moved into second place on the NFL’s all-time rushing yardage list during the game.

The Dallas Cowboys' Leon Lett dives for a blocked fourth-quarter field goal attempt as Bert Weidner of the Miami Dolphins scrambles for the ball on Nov. 25, 1993, in Irving, Texas. The live ball was recovered by Jeff Dellenbach of the Dolphins. Miami kicker Pete Stoyanovich then made the winning 19-yard field goal as time expired giving the Dolphins a 16-14 victory.

Buffalo Bills running back O.J. Simpson rushed for an NFL record 273 yards against the Detroit Lions on Thanksgiving, Nov 25, 1976 in Pontiac, Michigan.

#2612. Terrion Arnold's lawyer seeks sanctions for discovery violation

Seahawks cornerback Terrion Arnold remains on paid leave with eight felony charges pending in Florida. And the case against him is moving forward.

On Monday, attorney Harvey Steinberg filed a motion for sanctions, arising from the alleged failure of the prosecution to timely disclose as discovery material.

The gist of the 13-page filing is that the prosecution withheld a statement from defendant Boakai Hilton until after another defendant, Arianna Del Valle, sat for a sworn, pre-trial deposition.

Hilton’s statement, per the filing, conflicts with statements made by Del Valle. By not having the Hilton statement, Steinberg was unable to properly question Del Valle about the discrepancies.

On the surface, it’s an easy fix. Steinberg should get another chance to question Del Valle under oath. At a deeper level, the situation (if it unfolded the way Steinberg alleges) speaks to the integrity of the process.

Prosecutors have immense power and discretion, which should be exercised at all times with the goal of doing justice. Sometimes, a blind desire to “win” can overcome the mandate to do justice, thereby corrupting the system.

The Hillsborough County prosecutor’s office is already dealing with an unrelated case in which “winning” may have trumped justice. A prosecutor recently resigned for failing to disclose during jury selection that the sister of a fellow prosecutor was in the jury pool for a rape trial. The woman ultimately served as the foreperson of the jury, which returned a conviction.

A new trial has been ordered, and the prosecutor who failed to disclose the relationship has resigned.

It all comes back to integrity. Are the prosecutors playing games in order get a conviction or a favorable plea deal, or are the prosecutors committed to justice in whatever form it may take?

If Steinberg’s contentions are accurate, it looks like someone may have been trying to sandbag Arnold’s defense in an effort to make it harder to draw helpful testimony out of a key witness. In a case like this, the cards should always be on the table — with no one trying to keep anything up their sleeve.

#2609. Cardinals fire defensive coordinator Nick Rallis after blowout loss to Chiefs: 'We needed a change, a fresh voice'

The Arizona Cardinals fired defensive coordinator Nick Rallis on Monday, a day after a 34-7 loss to the Kansas City Chiefs.

Head coach Mike LaFleur confirmed Rallis' dismissal in his weekly news conference. He said the decision to fire Rallis was made out of a need for a "fresh perspective."

"Nick's a guy that I have a lot of respect for as a person, as a coach," LaFleur said. "… I just felt in my heart this morning that we needed a change. We needed a fresh perspective, a fresh voice."

Senior defensive assistant Teryl Austin will take over as interim defensive coordinator. Austin has previously worked as the defensive coordinator for the Lions, Bengals and Steelers, most recently with Pittsburgh from 2022-25.

Sunday's loss dropped the Cardinals to 3-8. They've allowed 30-plus points in eight of their 11 games and rank 31st in the NFL with 29.4 points allowed per game. They rank 26th with 355.2 yards allowed per game.

The Cardinals have plenty of issues beyond their defense. They rank 25th in total offense (290 ypg) and 29th in scoring (17.4 ppg) as the owners of the worst record in the NFC.

Former Broncos head coach Nathaniel Hackett is Arizona's offensive coordinator. Hackett has had four previous stops as an NFL offensive coordinator, including for LaFleur's brother, Matt LaFleur, with the Green Bay Packers. Mike LaFleur acknowledged Monday that the Cardinals need to improve across the board.

"It's not been good enough collectively, all phases as a team. I'm in the business, and it's my job to find solutions, and this is one that we're trying to find. …

"We're all in this thing together. If you're a real man in this league, you're gonna look at yourself in the mirror first."

#2607. Week in Review: Signature win remains elusive, but that could change soon

Welcome to Week in Review: a Monday feature that looks back at the week that was for the San Antonio Spurs, takes a look at the week ahead, and more. Enjoy!

Week 4: Another undefeated week stretched the Spurs' winning streak out to 12, with the young core spreading the wealth. Victor Wembanyama put on a show for his second Western Conference Player of the Week award this season, beginning with finishing off their road trip with a blowout win in Phoenix and come-from-behind win against the Bulls. They then briefly returned home for an absolute beatdown of the Steph Curry-less Warriors, led by a season-high performance from Stephon Castle to move to the top of their Cup group, followed by a career-high 31 points from Dylan Harper to beat the Jazz and complete the season sweep (yes, already).

The Spurs seemed overdue for a challenge, and they finally got one in a Pistons squad that was shorthanded but still featured Cade Cunningham, who has been making his own early case for MVP. After getting out to an early 14-point lead, the Spurs offense fell off as the Pistons found ways to keep Wemby out of the paint, and no one else could get anything going. They also greatly suffered in the non-Wemby minutes, and Detroit rallied for the win. However, the biggest worry was Harper having to leave the game late after an awkward fall. While he is expected to miss 2-3 weeks with a hip strain, it could have been much worse had it been the groin, so they got lucky there.

It wasn't impressive, but the Spurs found a way to get back on track. Overcoming a season-high 21 turnovers and hot three-point shooting from the Clippers, they used strong defense and timely shot-making in the fourth quarter to pull away. Castle put up a classic "PG Castle" stat line of 21 efficient points, 12 assists, 8 turnovers and 4 steals (it was very much a case of taking the good with the bad), and the bench unit had one of its better outings of the season, with everyone posting a positive plus/minus, including Luke Kornet!

With Zion Williamson a late scratch, depleting the Pelicans even further, Jeremiah Fears showing no fear (get it?) by getting chippy with the Spurs and baiting them into a couple of technicals in an up and down first quarter. But talent eventually won out, and the Spurs rode another 50-point game from Wembanyama to comfortably put New Orleans away in the second half.

John Schuhmann, NBA.com — 1 (last week: 1)

OffRtg: 118.1 (4) DefRtg: 106.0 (3) NetRtg: +12.0 (1)

The Spurs' 12-game winning streak ended against the Pistons on Tuesday, when they also lost Dylan Harper to a hip strain. But they've since taken care of business against the Clippers and Pelicans; Harper's absence allows them to go back to last season's starting lineup, and they continue to have the league's best point differential.

1. The loss to Detroit was the Spurs' worst offensive game of the season, and included them scoring just 23 points on 29 possessions (79 per 100) in Victor Wembanyama's 14 minutes off the floor. Wembanyama has registered a positive plus-minus in every game since the season opener vs. the Thunder (minus-2), but the Spurs have been outscored with him on the bench in 12 of the 17. So he just went and scored 50 points (adding 18 rebounds, four steals and five blocks) in less than 32 minutes against the Pelicans on Saturday.

2. The Spurs have seen a drop in 3-point rate from last season, but that rate goes up with Julian Champagnie (the league leader in corner 3s) replacing Harper in the starting lineup. #2601. Bears vs. Saints Game Balls: Big Jeff Dominates Again

The Chicago Bears continued their recent winning streak on Sunday afternoon, taking their fifth game in a row (and third since acquiring Jeffery Simmons). This time, it was a 21-13 victory over the New Orleans Saints at a dreary Soldier Field.

Much like last year's game against the Saints, there was some lingering rain and gray skies throughout. But that didn't take away from the newly acquired ray of sunshine on the Bears defense, Simmons, who once again was a force of nature that couldn't be denied by the opposing offensive line.

The Bears offense started hot, jumping out to a 16-0 lead by the middle of the second quarter. But much like the team's previous game against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, the offense cooled off considerably down the stretch and relied upon the defense to seal the victory.

Most expected the Bears running game to get back on track in this one. The Saints came in with one of the worst rushing defenses in the league, but neither D'Andre Swift or the returning Kyle Monangai could really get things going. Salvon Ahmed, recently brought up from the practice squad, was the only running back that found much success (6 carries for 33 yards).

But the real shining star on offense on Sunday was rookie WR Thomas, who has had an up and down season thus far. Two weeks ago, he had a kick return called back on a holding penalty, while also receiving a brutal unnecessary roughness penalty (and later a fine, too) that stalled one of Chicago's scoring drives.

Thomas made up for it this week, hauling in two passes for 56 yards (tops on the team), both of them convert on third down. He also had one rush for 30 yards, and a 29-yard kickoff return.

Thomas' first catch was this 40 yard reception on 3rd and 17 early in the third quarter.

Previous to this, Thomas showcased his elite speed with a 30 yard pickup on an end-around in the second quarter.

And then there was this crucial third down conversion and wild catch in the fourth quarter.

Many Bears defenders had good outings on Sunday, but when it comes down to it, El Jefe showed why he's in the running for Defensive Player of the Year.

Simmons recorded three sacks against the Saints, taking his total up to five in his three games with Chicago so far. He finished the day with three tackles, three sacks, three tackles for loss, and three quarterback hits.

You cannot stop Jeffery Simmons. You can only hope and pray to contain him. But you'd probably fail.

It seemed as though any time the Bears needed a big stop, Simmons showed up. He now has nine sacks on the season, the most in the league among defensive tackles. As previously mentioned, he has five with the Bears through just three games. Last year, that number would have ranked third on the Bears for the season. He's done it in 12 quarters.

Simmons' total of nine for the year so far would already rank second among the 2025 squad (Montez Sweat had 10 last year), and Simmons still has seven games to go.

Honorable mentions on defense: DE Austin Booker, CB Clark Phillips III, S Dillon Thienemann, and LB Devin Bush.

Who would have received your game balls? Let us know in the comments section below.

#2599. Bears have gone five straight games without ever trailing for first time since 1985

The Bears’ win over the Saints on Sunday was their fifth consecutive game taking a first-quarter lead and winning without ever trailing. That gives this Bears team an accomplishment the franchise hasn’t achieved in 41 years.

The last Bears team to win five straight games without ever trailing was the 1985 Bears, one of the most dominant teams in NFL history.

That 1985 Bears team lost just one game, a Monday night classic against the Dolphins in the 13th game of the season, and after that loss to the Dolphins they never trailed in the final three games of the regular season, or in the two playoff games they won to earn a trip to Super Bowl XX. In the Super Bowl, the Bears fell behind 3-0 in the first quarter before winning 46-10, snapping their streak of five straight games without trailing.

This Bears team isn’t dominating quite like that 1985 team, but the Bears are currently on a very impressive run: They haven’t just won five games in a row, but they’ve scored in every quarter of all five games, the franchise’s first streak of 20 consecutive quarters scoring since the 1941 Bears. That team, like the 1985 team, won the NFL championship.

The 2026 Bears are playing like some of the best teams in franchise history. They’re jumping out to early leads and never looking back.

#2592. Game Preview: Suns seek continued road success against struggling Pelicans

Who: Phoenix Suns (8-7) @ New Orleans Pelicans (5-13)

Where: Smoothie King Center — New Orleans, Louisiana

The road trip marches on as the Phoenix Suns head to the Big Easy to take on a New Orleans Pelicans team that is struggling to find its footing.

The Pelicans are 5-13 on the season, with four of those victories coming during a four-game winning streak in late October and early November. Since then, they've gone 1-9 over their last 10 games. In their most recent outing, they surrendered 50 points to Victor Wembanyama, who assured us he wasn't stat padding despite continuing to chase 50 with his team leading by 24 points in the fourth quarter.

But the Pelicans remain the conundrum they always seem to be. On paper, this is a formidable roster, one built around size and length. Three-point shooting, as expected, remains a challenge, but when you look at the personnel, there's plenty to like.

As usual, however, injuries continue to derail their potential. Trey Murphy III has appeared in only 10 games this season, starting center Yves Missi has played seven, and Dejounte Murray has suited up for nine.

Teams possessing length and defensive versatility have typically given the Suns problems over the past couple of seasons, but New Orleans has been the exception. Phoenix swept the four-game season series last year, winning by an average of 10.3 points. Granted, that margin was inflated by a 23-point victory last November, but the Suns consistently found ways to handle the Pelicans.

On the other side, Phoenix enters this matchup feeling pretty good about how its road trip has unfolded. Regardless of what happens over these final two games, the Suns have already secured a winning road trip by taking the first three. Win tonight, and you're heading into Houston feeling really good about yourself. Find a way to beat the Rockets on Wednesday, and you'll feel spectacular.

While the Suns' starting lineup still hasn't fully hit its stride, the team as a whole is beginning to look and play better. There's an opportunity to take another positive step tonight by getting quality minutes out of that starting unit against a Pelicans team that currently looks discombobulated. That's the kind of opportunity Phoenix needs to take advantage of.

Mark Williams — OUT (Left Shoulder Surgery)

Ryan Dunn — QUESTIONABLE (Right Quad Soreness)

Bennedict Mathurin — OUT (Left Plantar Fasciitis)

Bryce McGowens — PROBABLE (Left Elbow Infection)

Trey Murphy III — PROBABLE (Bilateral Patellar Tendinopathy)

Dejounte Murray — OUT (Left Ankle Sprain, Bad Attitude)

Trendon Watford — OUT (Right Ankle Sprain)

Zion Williamson — PROBABLE (Left Thigh Contusion)

Typically, I'd say I'm watching to see what the starters do, because we need that unit to gel as the season progresses if the Suns are going to become a complete basketball team capable of competing in the Western Conference. But tonight, I'm actually going to be keeping a closer eye on the bench.

While the Suns rank eighth in the NBA in bench scoring, the Pelicans rank fifth. There's talent on this New Orleans roster, of that there is no doubt. There's a reason why, whenever hypothetical trades start making the rounds, people look toward New Orleans to see which pieces they might be able to pry away. It's because the Pelicans have numerous players worth pursuing. And no, Dejounte Murray isn't one of them.

You have Saddiq Bey, Derik Queen, who could probably average a triple-double if he were starting, and Jordan Poole. I'm not suggesting the Suns should go out and acquire any of those players, but they represent quality offensive talent that can put together a run in a hurry if you're not prepared.

So while my eyes will naturally gravitate toward how effective and efficient the starting unit looks, it's the defensive intensity of Phoenix's second unit that I'll be particularly interested in watching tonight.

The Pelicans possess one of the worst defenses in the NBA, ranking 27th in defensive rating and 29th in points allowed per game. Simply put, they're going to give you opportunities to score.

So how do the Suns win this game? Beyond making sure rebounding doesn't become an issue, as it seemingly does every night, Phoenix needs to take advantage of what New Orleans gives them. The opportunities will be there. It's a matter of recognizing them, capitalizing on them, and making a struggling defense pay. Efficiency is your friend. The Pelicans allow 48.7% shooting for their opponents. Go ahead and shoot 50% tonight.

The road trip has been laden with subpar competition thus far, and to the Suns' credit, they've stepped up and taken care of business against every opponent. In fact, of the 144 minutes played on this road trip, Phoenix has trailed for only 13 of them.

I expect that trend to continue tonight, perhaps without the same level of dominance when it comes to controlling the game, but with the same result.

#2588. NFL news, live updates: Micah Parsons reportedly set to return, 49ers waive Brandon Aiyuk

Week 11 of the NFL season is almost completed with the Cincinnati Bengals (7-2) and Washington Commanders (3-5-1) set to play on Monday night.

The week began with Thursday night's matchup between the Indianapolis Colts and Houston Texans. The Texans prevailed 26-3 as the Colts performed so poorly offensively that the team decided to move on from quarterback Daniel Jones and released him the next day.

Jones' next destination will be one of the NFL's top stories as Week 11 finishes and the season progresses toward Week 12. The eight-year veteran is expected to clear waivers on Monday and from there, he will wait to see what his best option is, according to ESPN. Among the teams that could line up to sign him are the Arizona Cardinals, New England Patriots and Baltimore Ravens.

The San Francisco 49ers defeated the Minnesota Vikings in Mexico City to close out Sunday's slate. With the 35-10 victory, the Niners improved to 9-1 to keep hold of the top seed in the NFC. The Buffalo Bills matched them for the NFL's best mark with a 26-9 win over the Miami Dolphins.

One concern for NFL coaches this week might be players celebrating touchdowns with backflips and front-flips. New York Giants running back Cam Skattebo and Detroit Lions receiver Jameson Williams each went airborne in their Week 11 games, surely making their head coaches cringe. Teams have seven more weeks to keep their players on the ground.

Follow along with Yahoo Sports for the latest NFL news, injury updates and more coming out of Week 11.

After missing nearly a year with tears to his ACL and meniscus, Micah Parsons is set to return to the Packers' defensive line this week. The star linebacker has reportedly been cleared to play as of Monday, per NFL Network's Ian Rapoport.

Parsons reportedly needed one final clearance on his knee before getting the green light, and will now make his debut against the Rams on Wednesday.

New York Giants cornerback Greg Newsome will be sidelined for "multiple weeks" with a high ankle sprain, head coach John Harbaugh confirmed on Monday.

It's still unclear if Newsome will need surgery or if he will land on injured reserve, which would knock him out for at least four games.

"It's a serious high ankle. It's gonna be one of those lengthy high ankles," Harbaugh said, via ESPN. "It's going to be multiple weeks."

For more on Newsome's injury, click here.

San Francisco is finally parting ways with wide receiver Brandon Aiyuk.

After a months-long saga around the receiver wanting to be released, Aiyuk was officially waived by the 49ers on Monday. That confirms reports earlier on Monday indicating that Aiyuk would finally be released.

Other teams will have until Wednesday to claim Aiyuk, who will become a free agent after he clears waivers.

Former Colts quarterback Daniel Jones was not claimed on Monday, thus making him a free agent.

Jones is free to sign with any team that wants him, and that team can pay him the veteran minimum.

The Colts still owe Jones about $20 million.

The Commanders have activated running back Jacory Croskey-Merritt from injured reserve, and he is off the injury report.

JCM will play Monday night against the Bengals. He hasn't played since Week 5 due to a groin injury.

So far this season, Croskey-Merritt has 239 yards and two touchdowns on 67 carries. He also has 40 yards on five receptions.

The Cardinals have reportedly fired defensive coordinator Nick Rallis, per NFL Network's Ian Rapoport.

Arizona's defense has allowed 355.2 yards per game this season, the seventh-most in the league. The Cardinals' allowing 29.4 points per game is the second-most in the league, trailing only the Raiders at 29.7 points per game.

San Francisco 49ers general manager John Lynch has agreed to a multi-year contract extension with the team, according to reports.

Lynch and team owner Jed York agreed to the new contract with a handshake while on the sideline at Estadio Banorte before Sunday night's 35-10 win over the Minnesota Vikings in Mexico City, Fox Sports' Jay Glazer reported.

Exact terms of Lynch's extension have not yet been reported. The 49ers have not officially announced the agreement. Lynch's current contract was set to expire after this season.

Lynch's new deal joins an extension for head coach Kyle Shanahan, who reached agreement on the contract in September shortly after the 49ers played the Los Angeles Rams in Melbourne, Australia. San Francisco's international games this season have been extremely lucrative for the team's top football authority figures.

Rams head coach Sean McVay said Monday that tight end Terrance Ferguson will need season-ending surgery on his ankle.

Ferguson is the latest Rams player to be dealing with a long-term injury. Wide receiver Puka Nacua will also miss the remainder of the season due to a knee injury. Davante Adams has been sidelined since Week 6, though he is expected back by mid-December.

Ferguson's season ends with him playing in just three games. He finished with 63 yards and a touchdown on seven receptions.

The San Francisco 49ers are reportedly releasing veteran wide receiver Brandon Aiyuk, per ESPN's Adam Schefter.

Aiyuk missed the entire 2025 NFL season after recovering from a knee injury he suffered in 2024, just months after signing a four-year, $120 million extension with the team. He suffered a torn ACL and MCL in late October 2024 and hasn't played a snap in the league since.

After being placed on the physically unable to perform (PUP) list to start the year, reports later emerged that Aiyuk failed to participate in team meetings, and the Niners were frustrated with the "lack of communication." Eventually, he was placed on the Reserve/Left Squad list in December due to his continued absence and lack of communication with the team.

If the New England Patriots are interested in adding quarterback Daniel Jones, head coach Mike Vrabel isn't saying so.

While Jones waits to clear waivers, the Patriots named Tommy DeVito as their starting QB for Week 12's matchup with the Los Angeles Chargers. However, even if New England signed Jones, he would be unlikely to take the field with them so soon after joining the team.

Taking over after Drake Maye was injured in Week 10's game versus the Detroit Lions, DeVito completed 12 of 24 passes for 81 yards with 1 touchdown and 1 interception.

"We're excited about that, good preseason, and Tommy's improved," Vrabel said at his Monday press conference.

"I know that going into the last game, I think that being thrown in there and had some good plays, had some things that he can improve on and little things," he added. "I think that was probably the biggest thing is just saying, 'Hey, getting back into game action. How do you work in the pocket?' These are things that he got so much better on when he got here."

Green Bay Packers linebacker Micah Parsons "did well" in Sunday's padded practice session, according to coach Matt LaFleur.

However, the team will wait until after Tuesday's practice to determine if Parsons can play in Wednesday's matchup with the Los Angeles Rams.

The status of offensive lineman Sean Rhyan (high ankle sprain) and linebacker Zaire Franklin (shin) are also still to be determined. Rhyan has been out since Week 7, while Franklin has been sidelined since Week 6.

Running back Josh Jacobs (fractured finger) is unlikely to play Wednesday, but is doing individual drills to maintain conditioning, LaFleur said.

Fernando Mendoza's first career NFL touchdown pass is now in the books.

#2584. Luka Dončić gave a ‘strong endorsement’ of Quentin Grimes before free agency

Two seasons ago, Quentin Grimes and Luka Dončić shared the floor for 21 games and 228 minutes as members of the Dallas Mavericks before Dončić got injured and the two were ultimately both traded away in separate deals. During those minutes, Dallas outscored its opponents by 37 points.

Apparently, that was all the time and success necessary for Grimes to earn Dončić's trust as the Slovenian superstar pushed for the Los Angeles Lakers to sign him in free agency this past summer, according to Marc Stein.

"League sources say that Grimes, like new Lakers big man Walker Kessler, received a very strong endorsement from Dončić when the Lakers were assembling their offseason plans to make the 26-year-old one of their primary free agent targets," Stein wrote in his Substack, The Stein Line.

Aside from having Dončić in his corner, Grimes was also backed by head coach JJ Redick. Those are a couple of pretty powerful allies.

"And that gave Grimes two significant purple-and-gold advocates: Face of the Franchise and Lakers coach JJ Redick," Stein wrote. "There was confidence within the organization that Grimes could not only bring a trusted catch-and shoot prowess to Lakerland but also play more consistently closer to the level that resulted in the 6 foot-4 guard averaging 21.9 points per game for Philadelphia across the final 28 games of the 2024-25 season."

Thus far, that confidence has been rewarded. Following a slower start to the year, Grimes is playing excellently, averaging 12.7 points, 3.5 rebounds and 2.9 assists. He's shooting 41.2% beyond the arc and 56.9% on 2-pointers, and dropped a career-high 47 points in a win over the Charlotte Hornets on Tuesday.

Since joining the starting lineup in place of an injured Austin Reaves four games ago, he's averaging 25.5 points, 6.0 rebounds and 3.8 assists while shooting 57.1% from deep. That ability to scale up offensively is affirming the organization's confidence in him replicating "the level that resulted in the 6 foot-4 guard averaging 21.9 points per game for Philadelphia across the final 28 games of the 2024-25 season," as Stein reported.

Grimes and the Lakers return to the floor Monday night against the Utah Jazz at 7 p.m.

#2581. Report: NFL Primetime documentary is in the works

The recent passing of Tom Jackson has sparked much discussion about ESPN’s NFL Primetime, which was for years a mandatory Sunday evening destination for football fans everywhere.

As it turns out, a documentary is coming regarding the show.

Via Sam Neumann of Awful Announcing, the final product is believed to be on track for a release in connection with the Super Bowl, which is being televised by ESPN and ABC.

It could be part of the game-day programming. Three years ago, CBS debuted You Are Looking Live! — a documentary about The NFL Today — before the launch of the official pregame show in advance of Super Bowl LVIII.

For those who were actively following the NFL in the late ‘80s, NFL Primetime provided the first opportunity to see extended highlights of NFL games on the day they were played. Years before the Internet, social media, Sunday Ticket, and RedZone, Primetime became appointment viewing for fans who wanted to see more about what was happening beyond the two or three games available in their local markets on Sunday afternoon.

And the team of Chris Berman and Tom Jackson became the tour guides for the opportunity to essentially watch all of the important plays from every game in a compressed but meaningful package, with Berman’s cadence and the music accompanying the words creating the loose impression that it was all happening live. Even though everyone knew it wasn’t.

It became a unique moment in time, which at the time didn’t seem to have a shelf life. It’s just the way things were, with fans having no concept that there would ever be a way to watch all of the games live or to see any and all relevant plays long before 7:00 p.m. ET. It was a new frontier that no one had reason to believe would not remain a permanent fixture of each and every NFL Sunday.

As Neumann explains it, Jackson recently made a surprise return to ESPN as part of the filming of the documentary. ESPN shared footage of the reunion on Sunday.

It’s worth your time to watch it, if you were one of the millions who climbed aboard the Primetime Express every Sunday night of football season for something much more meaningful than a glimpse of the entire day of NFL action. And the documentary will undoubtedly bring back fond memories of the final years before advances in technology caused a narrow range of football options to explode into today’s endless menu of choices.

#2578. Las Vegas Grand Prix Data Shows Wild Chaos And Missed Wins

The 2026 Las Vegas Grand Prix turned into a chaotic mess where drivers swapped places constantly. The teams and drivers fought for the lead on nearly every single lap. Max Verstappen lost the top spot to George Russell on lap two but took it back right away. The official lap chart only counts a lead change when it sticks, so Russell did not get the lead until lap 28 after the Safety Car came out. This back-and-forth action made the race feel like a yo-yo that never stopped moving.

Isack Hadjar proved that breaking free from the pack leads to the fastest speeds. After he pitted for a new front wing, he set the fastest lap time for eight straight laps. Liam Lawson from Racing Bulls actually posted the quickest lap of the entire event with a time of 1 minute and 35.591 seconds. His average speed hit 229.73 kph, which was faster than anyone else on the track.

Mercedes had a chance to win but lost it due to a late mistake by George Russell. He passed Antonelli on the second-to-last lap but locked up his tires and hit the barriers. This crash dropped him from third place all the way down to ninth place on the final standings list. The team felt they had a shot at the win before that crash happened.

Antonelli tried to save the day but ran out of battery power at the worst possible time. He managed to pass the two McLaren cars and Pierre Gasly to run in third place before the final laps. He then passed his teammate Russell until that crash occurred. On the last lap, he tried to use his energy to attack Verstappen but had almost no power left. He finished fourth, just holding off Gasly. Andrew Shovlin, Trackside Engineering Director, noted, "We know we could have done a better job today and we will look at those moments, learn from them and aim to finish the final two races of the season more strongly than we did today."

The race finished with a change in the top three positions. Oscar Piastri and Lando Norris from McLaren capitalized on the chaos to secure their spots on the podium. Piastri recorded a fastest lap of 1:36.334 while Norris posted a time of 1:36.182. The data confirms that the slipstream effect was massive, making the order change constantly throughout the night. Drivers had to be very smart with their energy and positioning to survive the night.

George Russell admitted he regretted nothing even though the result was painful for the team. He felt the move to pass Antonelli was necessary to fight for the win. The Italian driver did well to hold off Gasly and stay in fourth place despite the energy issues. Formula 1 Official sources confirm that there are two races left in the season for teams to finish strongly.

#2577. Mike LaFleur: Defense needed a fresh voice

Cardinals head coach Mike LaFleur made a significant change to his coaching staff on Monday.

Defensive coordinator Nick Rallis was dismissed a day after the Cardinals gave up 435 yards in a 34-7 loss to the Chiefs. They lost 34-6 to the Rams the prior week and LaFleur said the team is trying to find solutions for a unit that hasn’t “stopped the bleeding enough.

#2575. Dan Campbell provides promising update after Kerby Joseph’s 1st game back

Last week, Detroit Lions coach Dan Campbell said the real tell about Kerby Joseph's return to the lineup will be how he feels after the game. The knee injury that held him out for over a year wasn't going to be as much of a problem on Sunday as it may be after playing on it for three hours.

But Campbell provided some great news on Monday. The Lions coach said Joseph came out of Sunday's win over the Tampa Bay Buccaneers with no cause for concern the day after.

"I think pretty good here. There's no red flags," Campbell said. "So that's a good sign."

Joseph played 46 defensive snaps on Sunday as part of Detroit's three-safety looks vs. the Bucs. He regularly manned the deep section of the field, while Brian Branch dropped down to nickel, and veteran Chuck Clark roamed the entirety of the field. While Joseph finished with just two tackles, Campbell said there were ups and downs to his afternoon.

"He'll be better for those reps, just like Branch was, to get his first reps of the season," Campbell said. "So, I thought he did some good things. There are things that he's going to only just get better at now that he's been out there. I thought it was pretty good. When you're able to get he and BB on the field and you've got Chuck out there, it's a pretty good unit."

After the game, Joseph told reporters he felt no discomfort in his knee for the entirety of the game.

"Every time I come out here, I feel like myself," Joseph said. "I don't know why you keep asking that. I'm going to always be me. I'm going to forever be me."

At this point, it appears Joseph is on track to play on a short week against the Chicago Bears, but we'll know more when the team drops their first injury report of the week on Monday. Detroit is only expected to conduct walkthroughs this week, so participation levels will be estimated.

#2571. FSU hires Georgia DC Glenn Schumann as head coach

The Florida State Seminoles have finally made their decision. According to a report from Pete Thamel and Andrea Adlenson of ESPN, they have hired Georgia Bulldogs' defensive coordinator Glenn Schumann to be their next head coach.

The deal is reportedly for five years. According to Thamel, Schumann is expected to stay with Georgia through the end of the regular season and postseason. The Bulldogs are currently the No. 1 team in the country and primed for anothr deep run in the College Football Playoffs.

Once FSU fired Mike Norvell, a plethora of names were linked to the head coaching vacancy in Tallahassee. Jake Dickert of the Wake Forest Demon Deacons, Manny Diaz of the Duke Blue Devils, and even former Seminoles' head coach Jimbo Fisher were names that were floating around. However, it became clear over the last few days that Schumann was the focus, especially after FSU met with him on Sunday.

He began his coaching career as a student assistant with the Alabama Crimson Tide in 2008 and kept that role through 2011 when he graduated with a Bachelor of Arts degree. After that, he was a graduate assistant at Alabama through 2014, earning a Master's degree in Sports Management in 2013. He was also the Director of Football Operations from 2014-2015.

Schumann worked closely with former Alabama coach Nick Saban and Kirby Smart, who was the defensive coordinator there at the time, helping install the weekly defensive game plan for the Crimson Tide. He was apart of four SEC championship teams and four national championship teams at Alabama.

When Smart was hired as the head coach at Georgia in 2016, Schumann came along as the inside linebackers coach, a position he held through the 2018 season. From 2019 to 2023, Schumann kept his position as the inside linebackers coach, but he was also the co-defensive coordinator. From 2024 to the present, Schumann has been the defensive coordinator and inside linebackers coach at Georgia.

The Bulldogs have had unbelievable success since Schumann came to Athens along with Smart. They've won four SEC titles and two national championships over that span. Since Schumann has held the co-defensive coordinator title or been the head guy, Georgia has been excellent defensively. They were second and fifth in total defense in 2021 and 2022 while winning back-to-back national titles. They were ninth in 2023, 30th in 2024, 14th in 2025, and they're sixth in total defense in 2026.

Schumann is from Valdosta, Georgia. That's in the southern part of the state, which is prime recruiting grounds for Florida State. Recruiting has been problematic for FSU for quite some time, and the hope is that Schumann can help immensely with that. Not just with his ties to southern Georgia, but with the overall recruiting process and all the connections he's made throughout his career.

Florida State will now look to build a staff around Schumann and get the program back to national relevancy. A new era in Seminoles' football starts now.

#2567. Lapel players, coaches soaking up state finals moment

LAPEL — For the first time in program history, Lapel's football team will play for the state championship when they face top-ranked and defending Class 1A state champion South Putnam at Lucas Oil Stadium at 11 a.m. Friday morning.

They players know what is in front of them and are focused on playing for their town and teammates. They are a focus and goal-oriented group.

But that does not mean they won't take a moment at practice Wednesday or before Friday's kickoff to enjoy the moment.

"We're going to soak in all of it," senior defensive back Reed Hamilton said. "This is our last game (together) ever."

Coach Tim Miller smiles at the though of reprising Gene Hackman's scene in Hoosiers when he measured the height of the rim at Hinkle Fieldhouse and showed them it was the same as their tiny gym in the fictional town of Hickory.

He believes his kids will understand that 100 yards in Lapel equals 100 yards in Indianapolis.

"Wednesday (practice) is as much about letting them soak that in and knowing they are playing where the Colts play," he said. "For any life experiences – a vacation, a hike, whatever – it's important that you soak in those moments. Life isn't always lived in Facebook, you have to experience it. They've earned the trip, I hope they soak in every minute of it."

For 24 Lapel seniors, this game is the culmination of a lifelong pursuit. It is born out of the hard work in the weight room, during weekly practices during the season and offseason workouts that started not long after the last season ended.

But they have earned the right to play in the home of the NFL's Indianapolis Colts as well as the right to soak up the experience.

It is also, win or lose, the final time two of the team's seniors will play for their coach fathers.

Running back and linebacker Jack Miller is Tim's oldest son and will play at Taylor University next season. While Tim's son Tate is a freshman on the team and his daughter Drew is one of the team's student managers, knowing that the last time he will share the field with Jack will come at Lucas Oil Stadium makes the moment even more special.

"For me personally, it was definitely the perfect year to come down here, my wife was pretty happy," Tim said Monday. "It's been nothing short of awesome and, in Jack's case, being able to coach him for four years has been an absolute honor and a pleasure.

"My wife's been a wreck, not going to lie about that. It'll be emotional and, even now I'm getting emotional about it. At the end of the day, win or lose, he gets to end his high school career at Lucas Oil Stadium."

Page's father Larry is an assistant for the Bulldogs as well — he coaches Mason's position, defensive back — and Mason plans on savoring that experience as well before he departs for Ouachita Baptist University in Arkadelphia, Arkansas to continue his own football career next year.

"I was driving by the football field last night and I was thinking, 'Dang, I played my last game there last Friday,'" Mason said. "At the same time, it's crazy that all the work we've put on that field, we get to bring here this Friday. That's what I told my dad, all that hard work has paid off in this game."

Tim points out that he did not coach his kids prior to their arrival at the high school level, crediting the town's Optimist Club program for developing the young talent in town.

But these four years have been just as special for his son.

"Mom was crying about it this weekend," Jack said. "It's kind of weird thinking about it that, no matter what, this is my last time being coached by him."

#2566. NBA viewership off to record start, national games up 37% from last season

NBA viewership is off to a record start this season.

The league announced Monday that viewership over the first month of the 2026-27 campaign is up 20% from last year on nationally broadcast games on NBC, ESPN and Amazon. National games are averaging a record 2.62 million viewers, too, which is up about 37% from last season.

The numbers are a solid increase for the league as it enters the second year of a new massive 11-year media rights deal, which will run through the 2035-36 season. The new deal extended games with ABC and ESPN, brought national games back to NBC and Amazon Prime Video entered the fold, too. Roughly 75 regular-season games are set to be broadcast on national TV each season, up from just the minimum 15 under the previous agreement.

The league also announced that viewership of live games on NBA League Pass and through the NBA app is up 50%. NBA Cup games on Prime Video are breaking records, too. Those tournament games are averaging about 2 million viewers each so far this season, which is up 90% from last season. The NBA Cup is in its fourth season of existence.

The viewership spike comes after a massive showing during the NBA Finals last season. The series between the New York Knicks and San Antonio Spurs averaged roughly 20.6 million views on ABC and ESPN, which made it the most-watched NBA Finals in nearly three decades.

Viewership numbers are calculated through Nielsen, which shifted to a new methodology in recent years that pairs both big data from smart TV and traditional panel boxes.

While the season still has a long way to go to live up to the NBA Finals numbers that the Knicks and Spurs drew last spring, it's clear that the league's new media deal is off to a very impressive start.

#2564. Dwyane Wade Backs Davion Mitchell’s Hard Work And Rise

Dwyane Wade is not just watching from the sidelines anymore. The Heat legend is loud and clear about his support for Davion Mitchell. Wade says he is "rocking" with the guard because of the non-stop work Mitchell puts in. This isn't just praise for a good game. It is about the daily grind that most fans never see. The 28-year-old joined the team as part of the Jimmy Butler trade, and his numbers prove he belongs.

At present, Mitchell is averaging 8.6 assists and 17 points. He shoots 51% from the field and 43.3% from deep. These are not small jumps from his past seasons. He went from 9 points a game to 17. That change has helped the offense huge. Per Yahoo, Wade highlighted the effort on his YouTube channel. "A guy that walks around and travel with a basketball everywhere he goes as a grown man, I'm rocking with him," Wade said. He noted that Mitchell always has a ball with him in the summer. That kind of habit shows why he is trusted so much now.

The Heat are on a seven-game winning streak. Mitchell is a big reason for this run. He started alongside Giannis Antetokounmpo, Bam Adebayo, and Klay Thompson. His defense is also top-tier in the league. Before the season, people questioned his playmaking. Now, he has proved them wrong. Wade pointed out how Mitchell ran the offense well against Cleveland. The team jumped from 10th to 4th in the NBA Power Rankings after their recent homestand. According to Yahoo Sports, the Heat now average 126.7 points during this streak. They have the highest-scoring offense in the league right now.

Bam Adebayo also stepped up when Giannis got hurt. Adebayo recorded a triple-double with 24 points, 15 rebounds, and 12 assists. That 12-assist mark is a new career-high for him. "When one of your best players go out the game, the next player has to step up. That was me. So we took care of business," Adebayo said. The team is moving fast and sharing the ball. "We getting stops. We running in transition. We sharing the ball and guys are making plays for one another," he added. This collective effort is what keeps the wins coming.

The winning streak will face a real test soon. The Heat must hit the road for three straight games against Eastern Conference rivals. They play the Philadelphia 76ers on November 25. Then they face the New York Knicks on November 27. The trip ends with a game against the Cleveland Cavaliers on November 29. Adebayo knows the challenge is huge but is ready for it. "It's going to be a gauntlet, but we'll embrace it. We'll try to play collective basketball. Try to keep this winning streak going," Bam said after the game. The Sixers sit at the top of the conference with a 14-3 record. LeBron James driving 16.1 points per game. The Heat will need every bit of their current form to survive this trip.

This is an article version of the CBS Sports HQ AM Newsletter, the ultimate guide to every day in sports. You can sign up to get it in your inbox every weekday morning here.

One of the biggest benefits of the NIL era is that college basketball has more elite talent than ever, now that players are returning for bigger paychecks instead of bolting for NBA money at the first opportunity.

That made selecting our 2026-27 CBS Sports Preseason All-America teams especially difficult, but our experts nailed it. Each of the three teams features players who will be performing at the next level very soon, but the best of those might be Florida superstar Thomas Haugh.

As our own Isaac Trotter explains, if Haugh can improve his range shooting, he won't have to wait long to hear his name called in the 2027 NBA Draft.

When it comes to how the talent broke down by conference, it was a a pretty level playing field for the most part.

Not to spoil anyting, but Arizona freshman Caleb Holt did not make the cut. He did, however, turn some heads in the Wildcats' exhibition game.

Loyalty is an excellent quality to have in a friend or partner. It's also why we love dogs.

It should not be quite as prevalent among college football coaches, some of whom have been undone because they did what was comfortable, not what was necessarily best for the team.

Our own John Talty highlighted five high-profile coaches who have been loyal to a fault, making hires and personnel decisions that have come back to haunt them. One of those coaches is Mike Elko. After a shaky season from Marcel Reed in 2025, Texas A&M chose not to pursue an upgrade in the portal.

Instead, the Aggies gave Reed a major payday, and they'll miss the College Football Playoff because of it.

Look, it can happen to the best of us. Dan Lanning and Dabo Swinney wound up on the list, despite the success that those two have had throughout their careers.

Steve Sarkisian is another coach who has fallen into the trap of being too loyal, but he may have a huge decision on his hands in the offseason. Arch Manning has struggled enough that another year in college should be on the table. If that happens, would Sark welcome back Manning with open arms, despite his shortcomings?

Finally, one person for whom loyalty is no an issue is Missouri QB Austin Simmons. After Trinidad Chambliss won the starting job at Ole Miss last year, Simmons didn't feel the need to stick around, but there won't be bitterness when Simmons returns to Oxford this weekend.

The Radio City Rockettes stole the spotlight during the Knicks' 123-116 victory over the Pacers at Madison Square Garden on Sunday.

Members of the famous dance company performed during the first quarter and captured the attention of Knicks legend Walt "Clyde" Frazier, who gushed over them on the MSG Network broadcast with lead play-by-play announcer Mike Breen.

"Hey Alan, if you need any help interviewing the Rockettes, I'm free at halftime," Frazier, a Knicks color analyst, said referring to studio analyst Alan Hahn.

"They're still here, Clyde, if you want to dance with them at halftime," Hahn quipped.

"I could show them the spots around the Garden, you know," replied Frazier, who played 10 seasons with the Knicks, from 1967-77.

"See now this is what I was talking about earlier that I'm worried," Breen said while laughing. "Your filter is starting to come off."

Pacers head coach Rick Carlisle explained that he had an interaction with the Rockettes that caused him to be late to his press conference after the game.

#2557. ESPN bringing Super Bowl LXI to IMAX theaters

This February, you'll be able to watch the Big Game on the Big Screen.

Disney announced on Monday that its broadcast of Super Bowl LXI will be available live in IMAX theaters across the United States and "select international territories," according to Variety.

The IMAX experience will feature ESPN's primary telecast (which, at least for now, will be called by Joe Buck and Troy Aikman), the halftime show headlined by Jay-Z, as well as pregame and postgame studio coverage. Moviegoers will start seeing promotional spots for the four-hour presentation this week. Ticketing information will be announced at a later date.

The news gives Super Bowl viewers yet another way to consume the game. ESPN and Disney have already announced a variety of alternate telecasts for the game, which is the first Super Bowl to ever air on ESPN airwaves. ESPN2 will feature an altcast with Peyton and Eli Manning, ESPNU will feature Pat McAfee and friends, NFL Network will produce an analytics-focused presentation, ESPN Deportes will carry a Spanish-language broadcast, and Disney Channel will have a Star Wars-themed animated altcast.

Movie theaters have collaborated to showcase major live sporting events in the past, including IMAX's recent presentation of the Formula One World Championship.

"The Super Bowl is a one-of-a-kind global cultural event imbued with spectacle, sound, drama, and heroes — all the makings of a great IMAX experience," IMAX CEO Rich Gelfond said, per Variety. "We're excited to work in partnership with Disney, ESPN and the NFL to give football fans an unforgettable night."

Memphis Grizzlies rookie Cam Boozer is expected to miss at least four weeks with an ankle injury.

Per the Grizzlies, testing also confirmed the structural stability of Boozer's ankle, and he's expected to make a full recovery. He'll be reevaluated in approximately four weeks.

In 16 games, Boozer's averaged 16.6 points, 9.2 rebounds, 5.3 assists, 0.8 steals and 0.8 blocks per game. As with most rookies, Boozer has room to improve his efficiency with a 41.7% field-goal rate and a 32.2% success rate from 3. But his dynamic offensive game as a skilled, floor-stretching power forward has translated to the NBA early in his career.

Boozer's impact has contributed to winning on the floor for Memphis. A Grizzlies team that finished 25-57 last season is off to a 12-5 start, which was good for fifth place in the West going into Monday's games. Boozer has emerged a a leader on the team alongside breakout guard Ty Jerome (24.8 ppg, 5.3 apg) as the Grizzlies look like contenders to return to the postseason.

They'll look to stay afloat in the top half of the Western Conference standings over the next four weeks without their standout rookie.

The Green Bay Packers star pass rusher has been cleared to return and will make his season debut in their Thanksgiving Eve matchup with the Los Angeles Rams, according to NFL Network's Ian Rapoport.

It will mark Parsons' first NFL game since he tore his left ACL and meniscus last season.
